subject: Streamline integration: request/response schema & streaming semantics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Subject: Streamline integration: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Hi Marta / Streamline platform team — thanks again for the product walkthrough today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the integration surface: 

1) Objective: integrate Redwood inference for multi-turn chat (customer support flows) plus an embeddings-based reranker for search. You want low latency for short queries (avg 120 tokens) and the ability to stream token deltas into your client.

2) Key technical asks you raised: SDK auth patterns (service account vs. API key rotation), routing (prod vs. staging / region preference), structured outputs & tool calling (JSON outputs + external tool hooks), embeddings/reranker architecture, and a few request/response schema clarifications (chat vs completions, tokenization, max_tokens, stop sequences, streaming semantics).

Attached is a first-draft schema (streamline_schema_v1.json) and a few sample prompts (sample_prompts.md) that map to our recommended fields. High level requests from our side: 
- Could you confirm whether your client will accept stream-delivered token deltas (SSE) or you prefer server-side assembly?
- Which authentication pattern do you want us to onboard first (service-account JWTs with short-lived tokens, or standard API keys)?
- Are there any hard constraints on response size (max tokens) from your mobile clients?

Proposed next steps: 
- You review the attached schema and comment (Marta) — by EOD Thursday PT if possible.
- Short technical sync (30 min) with your Tech Lead + our infra lead (Dylan) to walk streaming semantics and auth. Can we do Fri 2027-09-24 10:00 AM PT?
- I'll draft a configuration suggestion for Dedicated vs Hosted routing after the sync.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Streamline integration: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Thanks Ben — good summary. A few clarifying items from our side after looking through the draft schema: 

- Streaming: our web client can handle SSE-delivered token deltas; mobile teams prefer assembled responses to reduce re-rendering churn. We want the ability to flip between streaming and non-streaming in the SDK per route.
- Chat vs Completions: our support flows are multi-turn (so chat seems natural), but we also have a few single-shot summary/bulk-jobs where a completions endpoint might be cheaper. Can you quantify when to favor one vs the other?
- Tokenization: we use Unicode NFC normalization across the platform; curious whether Redwood token counts align with GPT-like tokenizers or if we should expect off-by-one in certain punctuation-heavy prompts. Any guidance on measuring token budgets?
- Max tokens / stop sequences: for safety we want hard caps and deterministic stops for end-of-sentence boundaries. Will Redwood enforce stop sequences strictly, and how does that interact with streaming?

Also: our security team needs an initial note on auth. We prefer service-account JWTs with short-lived tokens if Redwood supports rotating signing keys. If not, we can start with scoped API keys.

We will review the attachments and give inline comments. Confirming Fri 2027-09-24 10:00 AM PT works for the sync.

— Marta

Marta Lopez
Head of Platform Integrations, Streamline AI
marta.lopez@streamline.ai

(External note: ops+platform handles infra scheduling)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ops+platform@streamline.ai

Subject: Re: Streamline integration: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Marta — great questions. Answers below and a few concrete recommendations so you can test quickly: 

1) Chat vs Completions (how we recommend choosing)
- Use chat endpoints for multi-turn, stateful dialogues where system/user/assistant roles matter and you want token-efficient context reuse (we maintain role+metadata and incremental KV cache).
- Use completions for single-shot prompts, simple transforms, or bulk offline jobs (batching is cheaper on completions in many workloads).
- Practical rule: if you need tool-calling or structured JSON output with schema enforcement, chat + tool_calling gives better control and streaming deltas for the JSON envelope.

2) Tokenization guidance
- Redwood's tokenizer aligns closely with BPE tokenizers used by popular open models; expect small differences versus GPT-3.5/4 in some unicode edge cases. We provide a token_count endpoint in the SDK so you can pre-check prompt budgets server-side. Recommend adding a 10% buffer to your measured average for punctuation-heavy inputs.

3) max_tokens and stop semantics
- You can set a hard_max_tokens per request; Redwood enforces it server-side (request will terminate once limit reached). For stop sequences, our runtime supports deterministic stop handling in non-streaming mode. In streaming mode we emit tokens until the stop is recognized — clients will receive the final token delta indicating the stop; there can be a 0-2 token delay in streaming due to tokenization boundaries.

4) Streaming recommendations
- We support SSE with delta-encoding (token_deltas + role markers). For mobile routes where you want assembled results, set stream=false and use server-side assembly. You can switch at the route-level via the Console or programmatic routing rules.

5) Auth patterns
- Service-account JWTs with rotating signing keys are supported for Dedicated and Private customers today; Hosted supports scoped API keys with automatic rotation via the Console. We'll prepare a short runbook for your security team.

6) Embeddings & reranker pattern
- Produce vector embeddings (dense float arrays) from the embeddings endpoint, index in your vector DB, then re-rank top-k candidates server-side. If you want deterministic reranking inside Redwood we can provide a re-ranker pipeline that runs right after search to save a network hop.

Concrete config to try (suggested):
- Chat route config: model: open-llm-chat-1, stream: true (web), max_tokens: 512, stop: ["

"], tokenizer_buffer: 10% (SDK token_count checks before send)
- Completions batch job: model: open-llm-complete-1, batch_size: 50, stream: false, max_tokens: 1024

I'll post a trimmed example payload in the shared doc. Dylan — can you attach the short sample SDK snippet for toggling stream vs assembled responses on the client?

Ben
